PullRequest.Title: browserView: keep full-page screenshots from repeating the top of the page
PullRequest.Body:

On a page taller than its view, the integrated browser's **Add Full Page Screenshot to Chat** (shown when `workbench.browser.experimentalUserTools.enabled` is on) could return an image that repeats the top of the page instead of showing all of it.

This fix was part of #347643 and is split out into its own PR, as requested in review there.

### Why it happens

A full-page screenshot temporarily enlarges the page beyond its view. If the view is shown, hidden or moved meanwhile, or another screenshot is taken, that ends early, and the rest of the image repeats the top of the page. This happens routinely:
- The browser's Add to Chat menu and the Command Palette cover the page, so the page is hidden while they're open and shown again as they close, just as the capture starts.
- The workbench takes a placeholder screenshot of the page every second while it's visible, and another one whenever it's shown or hidden.

### Fix

A small helper, `BrowserViewCaptureGate`, coordinates this for the main-process `BrowserView`:
- Screenshots of a view are taken one at a time, in order.
- While a full-page screenshot is taken, showing and moving the view wait. Once it's done, they're applied in order, before the next screenshot. They're dropped if the view is disposed meanwhile.
- Hiding can't wait, or the page would stay drawn over the menu, dialog or editor tab the workbench hides it for. It's applied right away, after any changes held before it, and the full-page screenshot is then taken again.
- A screenshot that doesn't finish, for example because its page is busy or paused in the debugger, holds the rest back for at most 5 seconds, so it can't freeze the view.

`layout()`, `setVisible()` and `captureScreenshot()` go through it; their bodies are otherwise unchanged. The helper lives in `common/`, like `browserViewFocus.ts` and `browserViewCompositor.ts`, so it can be unit tested, since tests can't load `electron-main/browserView.ts`. The code comment that described this bug is removed.

### How to test

1. Turn on `workbench.browser.experimentalUserTools.enabled`.
2. Open a page much taller than its view in the integrated browser.
3. From the browser toolbar's Add to Chat menu, run **Add Full Page Screenshot to Chat (Experimental)**.
4. Open the attached image. It shows the whole page from top to bottom, without repeating the top.

### Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "**/platform/browserView/test/**/*.test.js"`: passed (135 tests, including the 4 new `BrowserViewCaptureGate` tests)
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "**/workbench/contrib/browserView/test/**/*.test.js"`: passed (153 tests)
- `node build/oxlint.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/common/browserViewCaptureGate.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserView.ts src/vs/platform/browserView/test/common/browserViewCaptureGate.test.ts`: passed, no findings
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- Manual check in Code OSS, on a 6000px-tall test page of 40 numbered bands, using the Add to Chat menu:
  - Without the fix, 2 of 2 screenshots showed bands 1 to 27 and then the top of the page again.
  - With the fix, 2 of 2 showed all 40 bands, and so did 2 of 2 where Quick Open was opened over the page right after the capture started. The page hid at once for Quick Open and showed again afterwards.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The periodic caller, interactive caller, Electron/CDP boundaries, new serial dependency, and exact five-second cap are all directly traced. Only how often capturePage hangs on a particular page is uncertain; the gate itself identifies busy or debugger-paused pages as supported triggers.
Findings.PerformanceResource: an Electron webContents.capturePage request and the interactive screenshot promise waiting behind it
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A queued interactive capture inherits up to MAX_WAIT_MS (5 seconds) from each unresolved predecessor; the normal visible-view path supplies a predecessor every second, with one active at a time.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: up to five seconds of added interactive screenshot latency before the requested capture even begins
Findings.PreviousBehavior: BrowserView.captureScreenshot invoked the requested Electron/CDP capture directly, so a full-page or area screenshot did not await an already-running placeholder screenshot.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every capture now awaits the prior capture's gate promise, regardless of whether the predecessor is a low-priority periodic placeholder and the new request is user-initiated.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `await previousCapture` at line 58 is the new head-of-line dependency; before this diff `BrowserView.captureScreenshot` called `_captureScreenshot` without a predecessor queue.
Findings.Title: Prioritize interactive captures over placeholder snapshots
Findings.Impact: If the page is busy or paused while the visible-view host's periodic capturePage request is in flight, Add Full Page Screenshot to Chat is blocked for the gate's five-second timeout. The full-page implementation is otherwise able to issue its CDP capture while paused, so this moves stale background work onto the command's critical path.
Findings.Evidence: WebContentsViewHost starts model.captureScreenshot({ includeDevTools: true }) and schedules another one second after completion; that request reaches Electron webContents.capturePage. addFullPageScreenshotToChat independently calls model.captureScreenshot({ fullPage: true }). The added await at line 58 serializes these paths, and the gate explicitly allows an unresolved predecessor to hold the queue for MAX_WAIT_MS=5000. The full-page path uses Page.getLayoutMetrics/Page.captureScreenshot and deliberately avoids a renderer round-trip when resolving display scale so paused pages are supported.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep full-page exclusion, but distinguish interactive captures from periodic placeholders so pending placeholder work is superseded or given a much shorter bounded predecessor wait; do not make a user command inherit the five-second background-capture timeout.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The frame-driven caller, IPC path, retained queue, synchronous drain, and native Electron operations are directly visible. Exact hitch duration depends on capture length, resize frequency, and device emulation, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: queued closures and synchronous Electron WebContentsView setBorderRadius/setBounds calls, plus device-emulation updates when enabled
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The retained queue grows with every editor layout event during a full-page capture, up to the five-second gate limit; continuous window resizing can contribute roughly one update per frame and all are replayed in one synchronous flush.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: a main-process rendering stall and visible resize/move jank immediately after the screenshot completes or times out
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each BrowserView.layout call immediately applied the current bounds, spreading native view updates across the incoming resize/layout events and retaining no historical bounds.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: BrowserView.layout now passes a closure to applyChange, which pushes every update into `held.changes`; finish then synchronously invokes every stale layout in sequence instead of applying only the latest effective bounds.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Line 45 newly appends every held change to an array, and the same diff routes each BrowserView.layout through applyChange; prior code called `_layout(bounds)` immediately and had no batch flush.
Findings.Title: Coalesce deferred layout updates before flushing them
Findings.Impact: Taking a slow full-page screenshot while resizing or moving the browser editor can accumulate hundreds of frame-level layouts. Completion then issues the same number of back-to-back native Electron geometry operations on the main thread even though only the final bounds are useful, causing a post-capture UI hitch.
Findings.Evidence: BrowserEditor.layout directly calls layoutBrowserContainer, which sends model.layout bounds over the browser-view service without deduplication. The changed BrowserView.layout routes each call into this queue. `_layout` invokes WebContentsView.setBorderRadius and setBounds and can reapply device emulation. The new array retains every closure and `_apply` drains it synchronously; MAX_WAIT_MS permits five seconds of accumulation.
Findings.Recommendation: Key held changes by operation and coalesce consecutive layout updates to the latest bounds, while preserving ordering around visibility/window-transition operations that cannot be reordered.

Scenarios.Scenario: Visible integrated browser placeholder screenshots, including a busy or debugger-paused page followed by a user screenshot command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The periodic placeholder capture is normally background work, but the new per-view gate puts its completion on the critical path of any later area, viewport, or full-page command; an unresolved predecessor blocks progress until the five-second gate timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send each placeholder or user screenshot request from the workbench renderer to the main-process browser-view service and return encoded bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per periodic cycle plus each explicit command; the periodic loop waits for completion before scheduling its next one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC requests existed, but an explicit screenshot did not await a prior placeholder request in BrowserView.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Periodic IPC is normally off the user path, but the gate makes its downstream completion a predecessor of a later interactive request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture the visible Electron web contents, optionally also capturing and composing docked DevTools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One main page capture per placeholder attempt, with an additional DevTools executeJavaScript/capturePage when docked; retries only for UnknownVizError.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary was invoked directly and could overlap a separately requested full-page capture; it was not a serial queue predecessor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A busy or paused capture can now block the later interactive command for MAX_WAIT_MS=5000.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active placeholder capture per visible host, restarted one second after completion; the effective problematic cardinality is one unresolved predecessor for the normal command path, with additional manually requested captures able to extend the serial chain.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The host itself has at most one periodic capture active, but user callers can overlap it. Before the diff those calls could proceed concurrently; the gate now serializes them per BrowserView, except that a five-second timeout releases the next request while an old request may remain in flight.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache avoids the predecessor. Each periodic success replaces the model placeholder; there is no negative cache or coalescing that lets an interactive request supersede stale background work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: caller frequency, new serialization, exact timeout, and Electron boundary are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal capturePage duration is page- and machine-dependent, and only busy or paused cases reach the full timeout. The exact prevalence is uncertain, but the five-second dependency and routine periodic predecessor are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: stale low-priority placeholder work can add up to five seconds before an interactive screenshot starts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add Full Page Screenshot to Chat while menus, visibility changes, or another screenshot affect the browser view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command awaits the renderer-to-main request, Page.getLayoutMetrics, Page.captureScreenshot, PNG decoding/transfer, and chat attachment. The gate can first wait for an earlier capture and holds show/layout changes until the full-page attempt finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request a full-page PNG from the main-process BrowserView and transfer its buffer back for attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command request; the gate may perform the capture callback twice internally after an interrupt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One request directly initiated one full-page capture without gate waiting or retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The entire IPC is awaited before image creation and chat attachment can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue Page.getLayoutMetrics and Page.captureScreenshot through CDP, then decode the returned base64 image.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two CDP commands per attempt; normally one attempt, at most two through the added interrupted retry before the five-second release.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two commands ran once; the diff can repeat them after a non-waitable visibility interruption.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both commands and any retry are on the screenshot command's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit command, normally one full-page attempt; a non-waitable hide can cause one additional complete attempt. Page dimensions are capped to the existing maximum output dimension.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Captures are serialized per view. A hide applies synchronously and marks the active full-page attempt for one retry; after five seconds, later captures may proceed even if the old attempt is unresolved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No screenshot cache serves this command. Placeholder images are separate and do not satisfy the requested full-page PNG. No cold/warm distinction changes the CDP command count.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: command, gate state transitions, retry condition, and CDP operations are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A retry's extra cost depends on whether the interrupted first attempt ends early and on page/image complexity. It is bounded to one retry and is required to produce a correct image, so it was not separately reported.
Scenarios.Verdict: The predecessor wait is covered by the latency finding. The bounded second attempt is an intentional correctness tradeoff without a clearly safer removal, so no additional finding was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or move the integrated browser editor during a slow full-page screenshot
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each editor layout still crosses renderer-to-main IPC immediately, but the gate retains its main-process closure. When the capture completes or times out, all closures are synchronously flushed on the Electron main thread before the next queued screenshot can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send current browser bounds and emulation data to the main-process browser-view service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call per BrowserEditor.layout/layoutBrowserContainer invocation; continuous resizing can produce frame-rate calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each IPC immediately applied its bounds in main and was spread over the resize sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: IPC arrival itself is not delayed, but each call contributes retained work to the later main-thread flush.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call Electron WebContentsView.setBorderRadius/setBounds and, when emulating, update device emulation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One native geometry update per retained layout event, all drained back-to-back after capture; only the final bounds are effective.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native updates were applied as each layout arrived, with no retained history or post-capture burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous burst blocks main-process rendering and delays the next gated capture.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workbench layout events during the capture, plausibly one per animation frame during continuous resize; at 60 Hz and the five-second cap, roughly 300 stale bounds updates can be retained for one view.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Incoming renderer layout calls can continue while capture is active. Their native application is serialized into one synchronous post-capture burst; no limiter or key-based coalescer drops superseded bounds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or equality check coalesces queued bounds. Device emulation deduplicates some identical derived settings, but WebContentsView setBorderRadius and setBounds still execute for every queued closure.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct frame/layout caller, uncoalesced queue, synchronous loop, and native Electron operations are all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact event rate and native-call duration vary by platform, and users may not resize during most captures. The queue permits five seconds of accumulation, so uncertainty affects hitch magnitude rather than the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: superseded layouts are retained and replayed synchronously instead of coalesced to the latest effective bounds.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced periodic screenshots, interactive full-page capture, visibility/layout coordination, timeout behavior, IPC/CDP/Electron boundaries, cache behavior, and effective concurrency. Submitted two findings: interactive head-of-line blocking behind background captures and synchronous replay of uncoalesced layout updates.
